title: Break-even: where revenue meets total cost
caption: Each unit sells for £50 against £30 of variable cost, so it adds £20 of contribution. Total cost starts at the £60,000 of fixed costs; the lines cross at 3,000 units. At the budgeted 4,000 units the gap is the £20,000 profit.
alt: Graph of revenue and total cost against units sold. They cross at 3,000 units and £150,000; at 4,000 units revenue is £200,000 and total cost £180,000.
description: Revenue is £50 a unit, a line from the origin.
Total cost is £60,000 fixed plus £30 a unit.
The lines meet at 3,000 units, £150,000: the break-even point.
Budgeted sales of 4,000 units are 1,000 units above break-even, the margin of safety, and earn £20,000 profit.

checks.name: revenue equals total cost at 3,000 units (£150,000)
contribution is £20 a unit (price £50 less variable cost £30)
